title: Munkaidő: When Work Starts and Ends

sections.title: kezdődik and végződik
sections.content: munkaidő ("working hours") is the word for the stretch of your workday. To say when it starts and ends, use two new -ik verbs that describe the thing itself starting or finishing, not a person doing the starting: kezdődik ("starts, begins") and végződik ("ends, finishes"). You already have -kor for a clock time and -tól/-től...-ig for a span, so you can plug both straight in.

items.english: My working hours start at nine in the morning.
When do your working hours end?

items.spanish: Kilenctől délután ötig dolgozom, utána szabad vagyok.
items.english: I work from nine to five in the afternoon, and after that I'm free.

sections.content: kezdődik and végződik only take a 3rd-person subject like a munkaidő or a film — for "I start work," say kezdek dolgozni instead, with the personal verb kezd plus an infinitive.
